draft.title: Hypothetical: 18 vs 24 t/s - What's Missing from Local LLM Benchmarks?
draft.body: This is a hypothetical exploration based on synthetic data, not personal experience. We're considering two hypothetical local inference runtimes achieving 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) on the same hardware with a single, identical prompt [F1]. While a higher t/s number like 24 t/s appears superior to 18 t/s, this specific hypothetical test setup has significant limitations [F2]. Crucially, factors vital for user experience, such as the time to the first token (TTFT) and the actual quality of the generated answers, were not assessed in this scenario [F3]. A model that generates tokens faster might still feel unresponsive if it takes a long time to start generating. Similarly, rapid output is less valuable if the content is inaccurate or nonsensical. This limited data point does not establish a definitive winner for all use cases [F4]. What other metrics beyond raw t/s do you find critical for evaluating local LLM performance in practice?
draft.plan: Introduce the hypothetical t/s values and immediately pivot to the limitations of such metrics. Explain that TTFT and answer quality were not part of the hypothetical test. State that this doesn't represent a universal conclusion and ask the community about other important performance factors they consider.

draft.title: Hypothetical Local LLM Performance: Beyond Raw Token Speed
draft.body: We're examining a hypothetical scenario where two local LLM configurations yield 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) respectively [F1]. This comparison was conducted on identical hardware using a single prompt [F2]. While the 24 t/s result is numerically higher, it's essential to understand what this hypothetical metric *doesn't* tell us. The hypothetical experiment did not capture the time taken to generate the first token, nor did it evaluate the quality or coherence of the model's output [F3]. A faster raw token rate could be misleading if the initial response latency is high or if the generated text requires substantial editing. Therefore, this specific hypothetical comparison cannot be generalized as a definitive performance benchmark for all situations or models [F4]. What aspects of inference speed, beyond tokens per second, are most important for your local LLM usage?

draft.title: Hypothetical Local Inference Speed: Beyond Raw Tokens/Second
draft.body: This post discusses a hypothetical local inference scenario involving two configurations, achieving 18 and 24 tokens per second (t/s) respectively on the same machine with a single prompt. While these numbers offer a basic performance indicator, they represent only one facet of practical usability. Crucially, this hypothetical test did not measure time to first token (TTFT) or the quality of the generated answers. A model with higher t/s might still feel sluggish if TTFT is high, or if the output requires significant revision due to poor quality. Furthermore, the observed difference does not establish a universal winner; performance can vary greatly with different prompts, system loads, and model architectures. These synthetic figures are intended to highlight the limitations of raw t/s metrics and prompt a discussion on what other factors users consider essential for a responsive local LLM experience.

Conclude by noting this doesn't establish a universal winner and invite discussion on other important performance factors.
